order.description: Sort by `created_at`. `asc` returns oldest first (default, matches the conversation timeline); `desc` returns newest first.

type.description: Filter to a single channel. `email` for email replies, `slack` for Slack and Slack Connect, `chat` for Microsoft Teams (and any future chat platforms), `live_chat` for in-app live chat sessions, `portal` for replies a contact leaves on the portal, `feedback` for the synthesized initial message that the thread was opened with.
type.title: Type

direction.description: Filter by message direction. `inbound` is from the contact, `outbound` is from your workspace. For live chat, `inbound` maps to `USER` messages and `outbound` to both `AGENT` and `AI`.
direction.title: Direction

user_id.description: Workspace user id. Filters to outbound messages sent by this user. Live chat messages have no user attribution and are excluded when this is set.
user_id.title: User Id

q.description: Case-insensitive substring search across the message body. Searches email subject and text, slack/chat/live-chat text.
q.title: Q

state.description: Lifecycle category. Distinct from `linear_status_id`, which selects a specific status within the category.

ProductlaneApiKeyCredential.title: Productlane API Key
ProductlaneApiKeyCredential.x-credential-instructions: In Productlane, open Settings → Integrations → API and create a v2 API key. Choose the read/write scopes for the resources your workflow uses: threads, contacts, companies, changelogs, tags, projects and issues; sending messages needs messages:write and internal comments need comments:write. Paste the secret without Bearer. The key's workspace is verified with GET /me.

channel_id.description: Slack channel id. Required for Slack threads unless one is stored on the thread.
channel_id.title: Channel Id

author.description: `user` (default) sends the message as your workspace user. On a `custom` thread nothing is delivered: `message.sent` carries the reply to your integration. `contact` records the message as inbound from the thread's contact. On email and live chat threads that triggers nothing; on a `custom` thread it works like an inbound email: the thread reopens, notifications fire and the AI agent may answer. Not supported on Slack and Teams threads.
author.title: Author

external_message_id.description: Custom channel threads only: your id for an inbound message. A repeat with the same id returns the stored message and creates nothing.
external_message_id.title: External Message Id
